rationale: Same drug class (thiopurines) for steroid-sparing in CD extends to steroid-induced remission maintenance in UC, representing the same clinical strategy across IBD subtypes
CD guideline's broader recommendation (thiopurine or MTX after steroid-induced remission) extends the UC-specific thiopurine recommendation for the same clinical scenario
CD guideline's recommendation for thiopurine-based strategies in steroid-dependent patients extends to UC thiopurine maintenance after steroid-induced remission
Both guidelines converge on limiting 5-ASA's role in maintenance — CD guideline rejects it entirely while UC guideline advises against adding it to anti-TNF therapy
Budesonide's limitation as a maintenance agent reinforces the rationale for thiopurine-based steroid-induced remission maintenance strategies
Both recommendations reinforce anti-TNF monotherapy for maintenance — continue anti-TNF if it induced remission, and do not dilute with 5-ASA add-on
CD vedolizumab maintenance recommendation extends to the UC post-cyclosporine rescue context, supporting vedolizumab as maintenance across different induction pathways
Newer AGA CD 2021 guideline favors biologic monotherapy over thiopurine monotherapy, partially challenging the 2018 ACG recommendation for thiopurine-based maintenance after steroid-induced remission
Newer CD guideline elevates biologic monotherapy over thiopurine monotherapy, refining the 2018 combined thiopurine/MTX ± anti-TNF approach toward biologic preference
Both guidelines converge on limiting 5-ASA — no role in active CD and discontinue after biologic escalation in UC, reflecting shared skepticism about 5-ASA efficacy
MTX is endorsed for steroid-dependent CD but recommended against for UC induction and maintenance, reflecting disease-specific divergence in methotrexate efficacy evidence
CD guideline's strong anti-TNF recommendation for steroid-refractory disease extends to UC where infliximab ranks highest among biologic options for naïve patients
CD guideline endorses anti-TNF for steroid-refractory disease while UC guideline defines post-anti-TNF sequencing, together delineating the anti-TNF treatment arc across disease states
Both guidelines endorse vedolizumab as an effective biologic — for CD induction and as a preferred agent in biologic-naïve UC
Vedolizumab is effective for CD induction but has diminished relative efficacy in TNF-exposed UC, extending understanding of vedolizumab's differential positioning by treatment history
Cyclosporine is explicitly recommended against in CD but endorsed for steroid-refractory ASUC in UC, reflecting striking disease-specific efficacy divergence with the same drug
CD guideline's strong anti-TNF recommendation for severe disease extends to UC where infliximab ranks highest among biologics for naïve patients, reinforcing anti-TNF as first-line biologic
Anti-TNF is first-line for severe CD while UC guideline provides post-anti-TNF sequencing alternatives, together defining the anti-TNF treatment pathway from initiation through failure
Infliximab is recommended for severe disease in both CD (severe active) and UC (steroid-refractory ASUC), extending the severe-disease indication across IBD subtypes
